correctness.rationale: Independent phase integration makes monomials diagonal with lambda_m,k=Q_k(a)Q_{m-k}(b). r_j(x)=Q_{j+1}/Q_j=1-1/F_j with a positive-term series F_j, increasing strictly in x and decreasing strictly in j. Thus neighboring eigenvalue ratio R_k=r_k(a)/r_{m-k-1}(b) decreases strictly with k, and each R_k=1 has a unique increasingly ordered radius. This proves every maximizing index and no triple top ties. Endpoint product ratio yields exact least eigenvalue. Uniform Poisson-tail expansion and Stirling with maximizing k=ma/(a+b)+O(1) give the stated constant, polynomial exponent and exponential base for fixed a,b. Independently recomputed bisection thresholds m=4,b=2 [0.858356,1.540129,2.576679,4.275695] and m=5,b=1.3 [0.452372,0.797944,1.3,2.087036,3.455017]; m=30,100,260 exact/asymptotic ratios approach 1 for (a,b)=(1,2),(1.7,1.7). Those samples corroborate but do not prove all-degree assertions.
residual_risks: Asymptotic applies to fixed positive radii, not m-dependent masks; squared-energy ratio is not ordinary singular-value condition number.
